name: charity: water
mission: charity: water is a nonprofit organization bringing clean and safe drinking water to people in developing countries. The organization inspires giving and empowers others to fundraise for sustainable water solutions. 100% of public donations are sent to local partners on the ground, who build and implement the projects. When the projects are completed, charity: water proves every one of them using GPS coordinates, photos and details of the community served.
theoryOfChange: Charity Water utilizes a 'monitoring and evaluation framework' called the MAP Framework to collect data across water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) indicators. This framework aims to understand impact, maximize effectiveness, and guide future funding decisions. The MAP Framework involves two types of data collection: Annual Check-ins, which are household surveys conducted at the baseline and endline of a grant, and Post-Implementation Monitoring, a comprehensive assessment of past funded work performed every few years. Their 'Our Approach' section details their strategy, including how they select water point locations, choose appropriate technology, vet partners, establish best practices, and ensure the long-term sustainability of their projects. They also have 'strategic pillars' that outline their objectives, such as providing safe drinking water, working with local partners, aiming for long-term sustainability, incorporating sanitation and hygiene activities, and focusing on rural communities in high-need, low-income areas.
